tweets.text:
I've been using Gemini 4 Neon and @antigravity all weekend and made a free video course on how you can get the most out of this combo.

Some takeaways:

1. Orchestrator and /swarm are very useful for planning and building with multiple agents. At one point, I had 42 agents running at once.

2. /grill-me is a great built-in skill that gets Antigravity to ask clarifying questions to help you flesh out the plan first.

3. Remote control is better than Claude Code's because every thread is active by default. I show you how to add Antigravity to your phone home screen to run this in the video.

📌 Watch my full 17-minute Antigravity course here: https://t.co/lmfSTiVBsm

keywords.definition_zh: 指反复改变或突然反转立场，通常带有批评意味。

tweets.text:
the predictions around the Jensen saga were a great demo of how little correlation there is between confidence and being right.

it’s wild how many prominent VCs, analysts and experts spoke with complete confidence about how things would play out .

some flip-flopped on their predictions within days - each time with the same confidence!

our info ecosystem asymmetrically rewards certainty, speed and brashness… “I don’t know,
let’s see how this plays out” just doesn’t get eyeballs.

worth remembering with ALL “expert” commentary you consume - people often have far less certainty than their tone suggests. they just form a view, stake out a position and say it loudly.

take everything with a sack of salt.

this news cycle was also a good way to calibrate on the people who are consistently loud and wrong.
tweets.summary_en: Confident predictions about Jensen were often wrong or quickly reversed. The episode shows how an information ecosystem that rewards speed and certainty can make expert commentary sound more reliable than it is.

tweets.text:
America can build the best frontier models and still lose the global AI race. Which is why Jensen’s return matters far beyond Nvidia.

Governments around the world want sovereign AI: models they can run on their own soil, on their own infrastructure, under their own control.

If American companies won’t meet that demand, Chinese companies will. Countries will start with Chinese models, then adopt Chinese infrastructure and chips. Having the smartest model won’t mean much if most of the world runs on someone else’s stack.

We’ve seen a version of this play out with Huawei. China understood that supplying the world’s telecom infrastructure creates lasting strategic influence. Once a country builds its networks around your equipment, it also builds technical expertise, supplier relationships, and future investment around it. Replacing that equipment becomes expensive and disruptive (the US government is now trying to finance replacement operations but it’s been difficult).

That’s why Jensen’s backing of the American open-model ecosystem is so important. Open models give startups the freedom to compete and give countries a reason to build on American technology.

We need both frontier leadership and global adoption. Open models are essential to getting both. https://t.co/f34FKKbljl
tweets.summary_en: The U.S. could lead in frontier models and still lose global influence if countries seeking sovereign AI build on Chinese models, infrastructure, and chips. Jensen’s support for American open models matters because they give countries a way to run AI under their own control while building on U.S. technology.

tweets.text:
Unlike say electricity, token demand grows in step functions as we find ways to put more compute to use on behalf of a single user.

auto-complete -> chat -> agent -> long-running autonomous agents -> swarms

Each harness innovation unlocks an order of magnitude more potential token consumption.

But then there’s a lag between these new tools and users figuring out what to do with them.

tweets.text:
This wouldn’t have sounded possible a year ago, but it’s becoming much more reasonable now that you can get 10X output gains based on the latest in AI model and harness progress. The result is that teams within the same company are driving very different levels of output based on how they’ve adopted AI.

This is a different phenomenon from other tech. Typically in the economy you think of technology adoption rates on a per firm basis, because the company generally adopts a relatively standardized approach to doing the new tech thing. Like “that company has gone digital or adopted the cloud”. So generally the uplift across teams is more or less the same across teams. 

AI is starting to look quite different. Even within the same company you can have a 10X delta between the lowest and highest adopters of AI and the impact they’re seeing. The teams that are able to actually figure out how to redesign their processes to best deploy agents in their workflows can see up to an order of magnitude jump in productivity depending on the job function.

Right now this is heavily concentrated in coding, but more work will become coding adjacent so we can expect similar results elsewhere too. This is going to definitely lead to some wild dynamics within companies.
tweets.summary_en: Teams that redesign their workflows around AI agents could see up to 10× productivity gains, creating wide gaps between teams at the same company. The gains are concentrated in coding today and could spread as more work becomes software-driven.

keywords.example_zh: 作者借用数学表达提出一个经验判断：用通俗语言解释产品所需的字词越多，定位就越可能不清晰。

tweets.text: The clarity of a product’s positioning is inversely proportional to the number of words it takes to explain what it is in plain language

builders.name: Nikunj Kothari
builders.headline_zh: AI 产业每一层都声称自己掌握关键控制点
builders.headline_en: Every AI layer claims to control the key bottleneck

points.zh: 他调侃 2026 年的创业融资叙事：应用、智能体框架、推理服务、模型、数据、基础设施、芯片和能源公司，都称自己掌握 AI 的决定性环节。
points.en: He satirizes 2026 startup pitches: every layer from apps and agent harnesses to chips and energy claims to control AI's decisive resource.

points.zh: 他借《料理鼠王》的台词提醒，杰出创始人、运营者或投资人可能来自任何背景，不能按固定画像筛选。
points.en: Drawing on Ratatouille, he argues that exceptional founders, operators, and investors can come from any background.

builders.summary_en: Every AI layer claims to control the key bottleneck
builders.summary_zh: AI 产业每一层都声称自己掌握关键控制点

slang.definition_en: Software that turns model capability into task execution.
slang.definition_zh: 把模型能力组织成具体任务执行的软件框架。

keywords.definition_zh: 在技术商业语境中，指掌握用户完成工作的关键流程和主要入口。
keywords.example_zh: 作者模仿应用公司的融资话术，夸张地说谁掌握用户的工作流程，谁就能主导整个市场。

keywords.definition_zh: 指提供模型运行与任务编排框架、让模型能力用于实际工作的公司。
keywords.example_zh: 作者调侃，这类公司把让模型真正干活的能力视为 AI 产业中最有控制力的一环。

keywords.definition_zh: 指提供模型推理服务、运行训练好的模型以生成结果的公司。
keywords.example_zh: 在作者模仿的融资话术里，推理服务商认为，掌握向用户交付模型能力的环节就能主导市场。

tweets.text:
2026 pitches in a nutshell..

App companies: He who owns the workflow controls the universe.

Harness companies: He who puts the intelligence to work controls the universe.

Inference companies: He who serves the intelligence controls the universe.

Model companies: He who builds the intelligence controls the universe.

Data companies: He who feeds the intelligence controls the universe.

Infra companies: He who keeps the intelligence running controls the universe.

Chip companies: He who controls the sand controls the universe.

Energy companies: He who controls the electrons controls the universe.
tweets.summary_en: A satirical roundup of 2026 AI pitches shows how companies at every layer of the stack, from apps and models to chips and energy, claim that controlling their layer confers ultimate leverage.

tweets.text:
One of my favorite movies is Ratatouille, and this is a quote I think of a LOT..

“Not everyone can become a great artist, but a great artist can come from anywhere.”

A good reminder to remember that generational talent can’t be typecast. The exceptional, by definition, defy the pattern. 

That is true for all folks (founders, operators and also investors).

builders.name: Peter Steinberger
builders.headline_zh: OpenClaw 聚焦稳定性，并推进新记忆系统
builders.headline_en: OpenClaw focuses on reliability and a new memory system

points.zh: 他称 OpenClaw 在高端个人用户和企业中找到定位，多人协作功能表现突出；团队近期重点是速度、可靠性和安全性，同时推进新记忆系统及 OpenClaw ID。
points.en: He says OpenClaw has found prosumer and enterprise users, while the team focuses on speed, reliability, security, a new memory system, and the upcoming OpenClaw ID.

builders.summary_en: OpenClaw focuses on reliability and a new memory system
builders.summary_zh: OpenClaw 聚焦稳定性，并推进新记忆系统

slang.definition_en: An advanced individual user with professional-level needs.
slang.definition_zh: 需求接近专业用户的高阶个人用户。

keywords.definition_zh: 在软件团队口语中，指把产品或功能发布给用户。
keywords.example_zh: 作者谈到持续交付稳定、免费的开源软件有多难，还提到了每天面对大量用户投诉的压力。

keywords.definition_zh: 指对工具有专业级需求的个人用户。
keywords.example_zh: 作者把这类个人用户和企业客户并列，提到 OpenClaw 在这些用户群体中找到了自己的市场。

keywords.definition_zh: 在 AI 产品中，指保存和检索历史信息、供后续交互使用的机制。
keywords.example_zh: 作者说团队的大部分精力放在速度、稳定性和安全性上，同时点出了新记忆系统这项功能。

tweets.text:
What a year this has been! Time to reflect and do a blog post over the holidays.

OC is in a great place, we found a niche in prosumer and enterprise adoption. The multiplayer team feature is best in class.

Shipping reliable and free open source is also really really hard, and waking up to countless user complaints every day is an emotional challenge. I’m glad the team is taking over most of the work these days.

We mostly been focussing on the boring part of ensuring things are fast, reliable and secure, with the exception of the new memory system and soon OpenClaw ID. 

To many more years!
tweets.summary_en: OpenClaw has found a niche with power users and enterprises, with team collaboration as a strength. Maintaining free, reliable open-source software has been demanding, and the team now handles most of the work, focusing on speed, reliability, and security alongside a new memory system and the upcoming OpenClaw ID.

vocab.definition_en: A tangible output produced by a tool or workflow, such as a report, image, or file.
vocab.definition_zh: 工具或工作流程生成的可查看、保存或分享的产物，例如报告、图片或文件。
vocab.example_en: The agent saved its findings as an artifact that the whole team could open.
vocab.example_zh: 智能体把调查结果保存为一份全团队都能打开的产物。

vocab.definition_en: A particular arrangement of settings or components.
vocab.definition_zh: 配置，指一组具体的设置或组件的排列方式。
vocab.example_en: We tested three dashboard configurations before choosing the simplest one.
vocab.example_zh: 我们测试了三种仪表盘配置，最后选了最简单的一种。

vocab.definition_en: To release a product or feature for people to use. If a product ships with a feature, that feature is included.
vocab.definition_zh: 发布产品或功能。短语「ship with」表示产品发布时自带某项功能。
vocab.example_en: The next version will ship with built-in search.
vocab.example_zh: 下一个版本发布时会自带搜索功能。

vocab.definition_en: A key lesson or insight you remember after an experience, discussion, or presentation.
vocab.definition_zh: 从一次经历、讨论或演讲中获得的主要收获或要点。
vocab.example_en: My biggest takeaway was that asking better questions saved us time later.
vocab.example_zh: 我最大的收获是，前期把问题问清楚，后面就能省下不少时间。

vocab.definition_en: Intended to make something clearer or more precise.
vocab.definition_zh: 用于澄清意思或进一步明确细节的。
vocab.example_en: She asked a clarifying question about what counted as a finished draft.
vocab.example_zh: 她追问了一句，想弄清楚草稿做到什么程度才算完成。

vocab.definition_en: To add enough detail to make a rough idea, outline, or plan more complete.
vocab.definition_zh: 为初步构想、大纲或计划补充细节，使其更加完整。
vocab.example_en: Let's flesh out the plan before we assign tasks to the agents.
vocab.example_zh: 我们先把计划细化，再给各个智能体分配任务。

vocab.definition_en: A statistical relationship in which two variables tend to vary together.
vocab.definition_zh: 相关性，指两个变量在统计上呈现共同变化的关系。
vocab.example_en: We found little correlation between how confident people sounded and how accurate their predictions were.
vocab.example_zh: 我们发现，人们说话时表现出的自信程度与预测准确性几乎没有相关性。

vocab.definition_en: A long, complicated series of events, often described with a hint of drama or humor.
vocab.definition_zh: 一连串持续很久、曲折复杂的事件，常带有戏剧化或调侃的语气。
vocab.example_en: What began as a minor disagreement turned into a months-long saga.
vocab.example_zh: 本来只是个小分歧，后来却演成了一场持续数月的风波。

quote.text_en: Make your confidence answer to the evidence, and let every good question sharpen your plan.
quote.text_zh: 让证据检验你的自信，让每一个好问题帮助你完善计划。
quote.author: Original

slang_glossary.definition_en: The California tech hub. In tech commentary, it often stands for the people or culture of the startup and venture capital world.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 硅谷。在科技评论里，也常用来泛指创业圈、风投圈及其文化。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A vulgar abbreviation for 'what the fuck,' used to express shock, confusion, or disbelief.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 「what the fuck」的粗俗缩写，用来表达震惊、困惑或难以置信，类似「什么鬼」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A blunt way of saying someone has stopped paying attention or thinking critically.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 直白地说某人不再认真听或主动思考，类似「脑子关机」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Shorthand for development or runtime environments involving local machines and cloud infrastructure. 'Envs' is short for 'environments.'
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 涉及本地设备和云端基础设施的开发或运行环境。「envs」是「environments」的缩写。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An isolated environment where code or agents can run with restricted access to the surrounding system.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 沙箱，一种隔离的运行环境，限制代码或智能体对外部系统的访问。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A storage layer for the state of a work or interaction session, such as runtime context or progress.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 会话状态存储层，保存一次运行或交互的上下文、进度等信息。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A storage layer for conversation data, such as messages and thread history.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 对话存储层，用于保存消息和对话线程历史等数据。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A queue where users review actions that need their authorization.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 审批收件箱，集中展示等待用户授权的操作。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Code that subscribes to a continuous stream of data or events and reacts as new items arrive.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 流监听器，订阅连续的数据流或事件流，并在收到新数据或事件时作出响应。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A usable output generated during a workflow, such as a document, code file, or image.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 工作流程产生的可用产物，例如文档、代码文件或图片。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An interface that brings together status information, metrics, or controls in one place.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 仪表盘或控制面板，在同一界面集中展示状态、指标或操作入口。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A service that uses the Model Context Protocol to expose tools or other capabilities to compatible AI applications.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: MCP 服务器，通过模型上下文协议向兼容的 AI 应用提供工具或其他能力。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In an agent system, a reusable bundle of instructions and sometimes supporting files for a particular task.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在智能体系统中，指用于完成特定任务的一组可复用指令，有时也包含配套文件。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Product development shorthand for including a feature or component when a product is released or distributed.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 产品开发用语，指产品发布或分发时自带某项功能或组件。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Available to use immediately with the default setup and no extra configuration.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 开箱即用，使用默认设置即可，无需额外配置。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A reset kept in reserve for later use. The tweet does not specify the exact redemption rules.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 预留给用户之后使用的重置机会。原帖没有说明具体使用规则。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A product mode intended to deliver faster responses or execution.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 快速模式，用于加快响应或执行速度。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal shortening of 'combination,' used here for two products used together.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 「combination」的口语缩写，这里指搭配使用的两款产品。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A component that coordinates tasks and manages work across multiple agents or tools.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 编排器，负责协调多个智能体或工具之间的任务和执行流程。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A group of agents working concurrently toward a shared goal. The slash form is the command mentioned in the post.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 多个智能体并行协作完成同一目标。「/swarm」是原帖提到的命令。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An AI system that can take steps toward a goal, often by using tools or executing tasks.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 智能体，能够围绕目标采取行动的 AI 系统，通常可以调用工具或执行任务。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A command that prompts an agent to ask probing questions about your plan. To 'grill' someone is to question them intensely.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 让智能体针对你的计划连续深入追问的命令。「grill」在口语中有「盘问」的意思。

slang_glossary.definition_en: To develop a rough plan or idea by giving it more detail.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 把粗略的计划或想法补充得更具体、更完整。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The ability to operate an app or agent from another device, such as a phone.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 远程控制，即通过手机等另一台设备操作应用或智能体。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A series of related messages within a single conversation.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 对话线程，同一场对话中相互关联的一串消息。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Automatically under the standard settings, unless someone changes them.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 默认情况下，无需手动更改设置就会生效。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A joking nickname for someone associated with resets. The post does not explain the specific reference.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 对某位与重置有关的人开的玩笑，类似「管重置的那位」。原帖没有解释具体梗。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A meme-style cheer declaring that 'Dot' is the best. The sample leaves the referent of 'Dot' unspecified.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 用夸张的网络口号为「Dot」站台，类似「Dot 天下第一」。样本没有交代「Dot」具体指什么。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A deliberately misspelled, exaggerated version of 'more' used in internet memes.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 故意把「more」拼错的网络用语，夸张地表达「还要更多」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Short for 'demonstration.' In the tweet, it means a real-world example that illustrates a point.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 「demonstration」的简称。原帖中指能说明某个观点的现实例子。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A long, complicated sequence of events, often discussed online as an ongoing drama.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 持续一段时间、情节曲折的一连串事件，网上常用来形容一场不断发酵的风波。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal way to say something is striking, surprising, or hard to believe.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 口语中表示某件事很惊人、很离谱或让人难以置信。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Short for 'venture capitalist' when referring to a person, or 'venture capital' when referring to the industry or funding.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 指人时是「venture capitalist」的缩写，意为风险投资人。指行业或资金时，通常指「venture capital」，即风险投资。

slang_glossary.definition_en: AI capabilities developed or operated under a country's or region's control, often emphasizing local infrastructure, data governance, or technological autonomy.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 主权 AI，指由一国或地区自主掌控开发或运营的 AI 能力，通常强调本地基础设施、数据治理或技术自主权。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In agent engineering, the surrounding software that runs an agent and manages parts of its execution, such as tool use, state, or permissions.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在智能体工程中，指用于运行和管理智能体的外围软件框架，可负责工具调用、状态或权限等。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A term for the core runtime or control logic that coordinates an agent's execution. Its exact scope varies by system.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 智能体内核，指协调智能体运行的核心运行时或控制逻辑，具体涵盖哪些功能取决于系统设计。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The capacity to choose and take actions toward a goal with some degree of independence.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 能动性，指在一定程度上独立作出选择并采取行动以实现目标的能力。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A blend of 'professional' and 'consumer,' often used for an advanced consumer who wants professional-grade features.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 「professional」与「consumer」的合成词，常指需要专业级功能的进阶消费者。
